clue.text: Boatman involved in crime gets coppers annoyed

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P for pence
annoyed means irate, cross

explanation.surface: The setter, Boatman, is mixed up in a crime and the police are cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boatman' looks like the setter signing his own clue, but here it means a seafaring robber. 'Coppers' are coins, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaborne robber is literally a boatman engaged in crime, a sea thief.

clue.text: Clarification sought on fate of band of good-for-nothings

parts.note: saying 'Sorry?' asks someone to repeat or clarify
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone asks what happened to a gang of wastrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase for a worthless or disreputable group of people.

clue.text: Commit crime, giving judge backchat!

indicators.note: giving here is read as giving back, the setter's 'back' doing double duty to send the words judge and backchat into reverse

parts.note: a referee, REF, judges a match
backchat is cheeky talk, lip

explanation.surface: An exclamation of outrage: cheeking a judge treated as if it were a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter said 'back' in 'backchat' does double duty as the reversal signal, with the exclamation mark flagging the liberty; 'giving' carries that signal here. REFLIP read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal small items is a petty crime, so it is to commit a crime.

clue.text: Criminal case led to clean up, resulting in loss of deposit

definitions.text: clean up, resulting in loss of deposit

indicators.note: criminal as in a criminal mess, so the letters of the words case led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal case is cleaned up and someone forfeits their deposit money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests money paid as security; it is the limescale left in a kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing scale, the chalky build-up in kettles and pipes, is a cleaning that loses that deposit.

clue.text: Caper gets student doctor locked up

indicators.note: gets ... locked up: the prison takes the doctor in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: locked up means in gaol, the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the first medical degree a student doctor works for

explanation.surface: A trainee medic is imprisoned for some prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' looks like the crime of the clue's theme; here it is a playful leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or frisk about playfully, a synonym of the leap word.

clue.text: Perhaps this is time for a criminal

definitions.meaning: the clue itself is a grammatical ..., so this clue is an example
the term of punishment a court gives a convict

explanation.surface: Musing that a criminal's time has come.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the grammatical unit of words and a judge's prison term share the word.

clue.text: After love setback I stole freely — no getting cold feet on these

definitions.text: no getting cold feet on these

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters after the turned-round love
setback means the word for love is sent backwards

parts.note: love is nil, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: freely means the letters of I stole are arranged loosely, in any order

explanation.surface: After a romantic disappointment, a thief helped himself, and nobody got cold feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' makes LIN from NIL; 'freely' rearranges I STOLE to OTILES. 'cold feet' suggests nerves; it means literally chilly toes on a warm floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum squares make a floor warmer underfoot than stone, so bare feet stay warm.

clue.text: Drugs dropped at start of getaway car's last lark

indicators.note: the drugs are dropped from the front of the getaway word

parts.note: a getaway is an escape
E is ecstasy, so drugs, plural, are Es

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of car's

explanation.surface: Narcotics are tossed out at the start of the escape, then the getaway car's final prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped at start of' removes ES from ESCAPE, leaving CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of fun or mischief, and so is a caper, a prank.

clue.text: Offer up newly scarce housing for one offender with another one

indicators.note: housing means the rearranged letters hold the other pieces inside them
newly means the letters of scarce are made anew, reshuffled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
read as off-ender: the end letter of off
a second I for one

explanation.surface: Scarce prison housing is offered to one offender who must share with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges SCARCE to SACRCE. 'offender' is split as off-ender, the end of 'off', giving F.
explanation.definitionFit: To sacrifice is to offer something up to a deity or for a cause, a synonym.

clue.text: One moves to lead in police patrols and gets involved in crime

indicators.note: the letter for one shifts to the front of the word for police patrols

parts.note: a police officer's patrol route is a beat
one is A, as in a single

explanation.surface: An officer is moved to head up the police patrols and gets caught up in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATS with its A brought to the front becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To help or encourage a wrongdoer is to become an accessory, involved in the crime.

clue.text: As from any remote origins

indicators.note: origins are the starting letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Something that comes from a distant source.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from distant origins means from a long way off, from a distance.

clue.text: Informant in bank job

definitions.meaning: one who tells, who passes on information
the cashier's post at a bank counter

explanation.surface: A police informer within a bank robbery gang.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tells is an informant; a bank cashier is also called by this title.

clue.text: Persistent criminal put inside to get free food

indicators.note: put inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to lig is British slang for freeloading at parties and launches
a felon is a criminal

explanation.surface: A habitual offender is jailed and so gets fed for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' suggests prison, but it is the container signal. Ligging is British slang for scrounging free food and drink at parties and launches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting a whole lifetime is enduring, persistent throughout.

clue.text: A cell where assault might lead

definitions.meaning: an electrical cell, a power source
assault and ... is a paired legal charge

explanation.surface: A prison cell where an attack might take place.
explanation.definitionFit: A power unit is made of cells; and the legal phrase 'assault and' leads into this word.

clue.text: Government by one in outrageous yacht, Russian sins denied

indicators.note: outrageous suggests the letters are thrown into wild disorder
denied means the letters of sins are refused a place and taken out

explanation.surface: An autocrat lives it up on a flashy yacht, with Russian vices kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges YACHT RUSSIAN; 'denied' takes away the letters of SINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute rule by a single person, autocracy, is government by one.

clue.text: Interpret what's set down regularly in freehand

indicators.note: regularly in takes every other letter of the word freehand

explanation.surface: Deciphering something written out by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sense of written words is reading them, interpreting the text.

clue.text: Mishap for police officer capturing ringleader

indicators.note: capturing means the officer word holds the leader inside it

parts.note: copper is British slang for a policeman
the leader, first letter, of ring

explanation.surface: A police officer's mishap in nabbing the head of a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' looks like the gang boss; it is the first letter of 'ring'. To come a cropper is British for to fall or fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy fall or failure, as in 'come a cropper', is a mishap.

clue.text: Arrested after sidekick lost nerve

indicators.note: after puts the arrested word after the sidekick word

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a sidekick or helper
nicked is British slang for arrested

explanation.surface: Once the accomplice is arrested, the criminal loses his nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seized with sudden fear is to lose one's nerve, a synonym.

clue.text: Detective lacks heart to present warrant

indicators.note: lacks heart leaves only the ends of the word detective

parts.note: to serve a writ or warrant is to present it formally

explanation.surface: A heartless detective turns up to serve a warrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warrant' looks like the legal document; it is the verb, to merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To warrant something is to merit or be worthy of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Look up to Scottish monarch, royal inside, one last European

indicators.note: inside puts the royal letter within the monarch word

parts.note: Landseer's painting The Monarch of the Glen shows a Scottish stag
R, as in Regina or Rex, stands for royal
A is one, a single
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Looking up to a Scottish king with a royal guest and a lone European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish monarch' suggests a king; The Monarch of the Glen is a famous painting of a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazing at stars means looking up at the night sky.

clue.text: Police officer solving crossword puzzle — would CPS's letters get ignored?

indicators.note: solving suggests the puzzle's letters are worked out into a new order
the letters of would CPS's are left out of the rearranged pool

explanation.surface: A policeman doing a crossword wonders whether the prosecutors' letters can be skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solving' rearranges CROSSWORD PUZZLE; 'letters get ignored' removes WOULDCPSS. The CPS is England's Crown Prosecution Service.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a policeman, from Liverpool usage.

clue.text: Consuming desire begins at home in middle age

indicators.note: begins takes the first letter of desire

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: middle takes the centre letter of age

explanation.surface: An all-consuming desire takes hold at home in middle age.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal is consuming it, so the participle fits the verb form.

clue.text: Condescends to speak of northerners

indicators.note: to speak of means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: Danes are northern Europeans, Scandinavians

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to talk about people from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to do something beneath one's dignity is to condescend, a synonym.

clue.text: Seize family at dinner — it's their cover

parts.note: nap is old slang for seize or nab
kin are family

explanation.surface: Diners grab their relatives as a cover story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' suggests an alibi; it is the cloth spread on a diner's lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth laid on the lap protects diners' clothes, a cover at the table.

clue.text: It's a fashion to speak of criminals

indicators.note: to speak of signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the Krays were notorious London gangster twins of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Talking about criminals has become trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kray twins, Ronnie and Reggie, ran organised crime in London's East End in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing enthusiasm or fad is a fashion.

clue.text: Means of oversight for every single police officer in the Home Counties

parts.note: per means for each, every
I is the numeral one, single

indicators.note: in puts the officer within the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East, SE
a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: Surveillance for each police officer posted around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's viewing tube lets one see over obstacles, a literal means of seeing over.

clue.text: Article contains information by which force gets criminal

indicators.note: contains means the article word holds the information letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the standard abbreviation for information
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A news article on how the police force catches a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is a kind of criminal, the general word standing for the specific.

clue.text: Give clean interpretation of the Gospel

indicators.note: an interpretation is a fresh rendering, so the letters of give clean are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to read the scriptures in a wholesome way.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, so the adjective means relating to it.
